When I was twenty five I started working for an in-home-care company in California. I hadn't been working for years because I had been a stay at home mom but times got tough so when a friend of mine told me that the place she worked at was hiring, I quickly filled out an application, was interviewed and hired within a week. The way in-home-care works is you live in the client's home or alternate with other co-workers to create a full time staff. You help them with basic everyday things like cooking, bathing and just getting around. You have to be very careful not to do everything for them because they may become dependant on your outside help and that’s not your goal. You're basically there to help them become independent even when that seems impossible.

The clients we got were usually shut ins who had no ability to socialize or function as normal people due to mental or developmental illnesses. One client I had needed someone to physically removed the poop from there (with gloves if you were wondering). This was not my favorite part of the job. My favorite part was helping people feel normal. It always made me smile when I saw in their eyes that they realized they could do something on their own. One of my clients who loved their Independence was a woman we'll call Doris. Doris lived in an apartment in the suburbs and had very little money for day to day things. Her apartment was filled from floor to ceiling with old newspapers which threatened to topple over and leave her immobilized. Her bedroom was cluttered with clothes and junk. More news papers, magazines and only half of the bed was usable. Her kitchen was the worst. Most of the other workers couldn't be bothered to properly clean, cook, or help her shop for foods that were both nutritious and tasty.

This was especially sad because even though Doris had the mental development of a child she was passionate about eating. Whenever she had the opportunity to go out even just for fast food, her eyes would light up like a kid on Christmas. Every time, I took her out (during these day trips I often spent my own money cause I just felt so bad for her, something I could have gotten fired for) she tried to order the largest thing on the menu and then something else for later. I would always laugh when I asked her what she wanted to eat. She’d always reply with something huge then ask, “and can I get something else?”

The fact that I took her out to eat and made sure her home food situation got sorted out made me her favorite worker. She often asked for me by name. This caused the company to swap my schedule around so that instead of going to other clients houses, I was often doing double shifts days in a row with Doris.

Now Doris had her issues too. She hated to bathe, change her clothes, never wanted to clean or even have others clean for her because that meant that something might get thrown away and she hated to throw anything away. But I had my tools to persuade her. If she cleaned herself, she might get a tasty lunch dessert. If she threw away some newspapers, maybe a hamburger at Wendy's would be tonight’s dinner. If she went out for a walk to improve her physical condition then I would make sure there were frozen dinners that were both good for her and good tasting in her freezer which I had made from scratch. We made a good team and I probably would have gone on helping her forever if it hadn't been for this incident which changed everything. Now, even with me and the other workers cleaning, there was always a fly problem in Doris’ apartment. The flies were inside and outside. Even with bug screens, they seemed to be drawn to the apartment. If you looked out the kitchen window, you'd see them covering the screen as if they were desperate to get in. The buzzing sound was always there. You'd get used to it, but sometimes when there was no other sounds you'd realize how loud it was getting. It really started to get under my skin.

There were other things too. Like one day I came early in the morning to do some light house cleaning before Doris woke up. Her apartment was always dark but more so in the mornings and it always made me feel uncomfortable. That morning though I actually felt like something was watching me. Not someone, I never expected to turn my head and see Doris or anyone else. It wasn't a person I felt, it was more like just a presence.

Another morning I had finished my chores early and had nothing else to do. Doris was still asleep so I turned on the tv and quietly watched the morning news. I glanced to my right in the darkness of the morning light and there over the lamp was a twist of brownish gray smoke that moved unlike any other smoke I had ever seen. It stayed in place until it dissipated into the air. It left no smell and there was nothing that could have been burning. The lamp wasn't on.

On another occasion, it was still night and I came in to relive the night worker. She was acting kind of weird but didn’t seem to want to talk about it. I followed her out to her car and she told me that in some of the rooms like the kitchen or the bathroom that something would fall and she would find things like shampoo bottles that were all the way over in the bath tub area far off in the bathroom sink. Now in case I'm not illustrating this properly, there was no direct line for those objects to have fallen naturally, they only could have been moved by a person or something I can't even imagine. The same thing would happen with silverware in the kitchen. All the dishes were washed by hand and the silverware which had been sitting in the drying rack pockets would somehow fall out and end up across the kitchen on the stove. Even though the stove and the drying rack are parallel to each other, the sound would be as if the objects had fallen with force.

One day in-particular, was very bad. Doris and I had come back from a walk and lunch. She had gotten a salad, and something else and was very happy about that. When we got home, she was tired and wanted to sit on her favorite recliner and watch TV. The flies were there in force that day. They matted the screen creating large blotches of clumps which kept what little light normally made it in out. We were watching an old western movie which was one of her favorites. And like normal, she fell asleep sitting up watching the screen. The snores came soon after.

I pulled out my cell phone, not wanting to wake her up and quietly texted a few of my friends about what we might be doing this upcoming weekend. Occasionally I would look up from my phone to watch the movie or to check on Doris when she stopped snoring thinking she might be waking up. She was never awake, soon after I'd look at her, the snores would come back and I'd go back to my phone. But once, this wasn't the case and it’s something that I wish I had never seen. I looked up and I didn't notice the screen at all. I couldn't even look at it because Doris was staring at me. Her eyes were full open with an awareness that I had never seen on her face before. There were no whites in her eyes. All I could see was darkness like looking down a hallway that lead into the earth. She looked at me and I was frozen in fear. I couldn't look away.

I asked her if she was okay trying not to let on that anything seemed wrong. She gave me a gnarled lunatic grin that looked as foreign on her face as the darkness of her eyes. My heart raced within my chest and I prayed without even realizing it to be anyplace but here. I looked around, suddenly aware that those were the eyes of imminent attack. She was going to attack me and I wanted to reach for something to defend myself. I didn’t find anything that I could use except a pencil on the table, so I grabbed it leaving her gaze for just a moment. When I looked back at her, the face was gone. Her chin was buried in her chest as she slept as if nothing had happened.

That was one of the last times I ever worked for Dorris. When I was asked to work for her I always made up excuses as to why I couldn’t. I stopped buying her treats and just became another faceless worker that was no different than anyone else. She even seemed for forget about me, no longer asking for me and before long I stopped being assigned to her.

I don't know what I saw that night, but if there is evil in this world I think it hides behind the sleeping eyes of people who have lost a grasp on reality. I have since left that field and have never looked back.
